structure.heading: Benchmark Baseline: Cycle Time, First-Pass Yield, and Capacity Utilization (Q1 2026)
text_content: **Benchmark Baseline: Cycle Time, First-Pass Yield, and Caapcity Utilizatoin (Q1 2026)**

The review baseline period is Q1 2026 (2026-01-01 to 2026-03-31). Data were extracted from MES logs and production schedules after harmonizing definitions for end-to-end cycle time, first-pass yield, and capacity utilization. Planend outages and discrete project work were excluded to maintain steady-state comparability across Plants A, B, and C for accurate benchmarking and subsequent lean opportunity identification.

Cycle time performance varies: Plant A median end-to-end cycle time is 6.2 days versus Plant C at 9.1 days. The 2.9-day spread increases WIP, elongates lead times, and ties up working capital at Plant C. Analysis highlights batch sizes, changeover frequency, and material availability as main contributors; targeted takt alignment, SMED, and Kanban pilots were recommended to reduce cycle time.

Quality and capacity indicators reveal prioritise: Plant B first-pass yield is 92.4% while Plant C is 86.7%, reflecting rework, scrap, and inspection bottlenecks that depress effective capacity. Capacity utilization was calculated against rated hourly capacity and shows scope to recover throughput without capital spend through rework reduction and process stabilization. Prioritization will fcous on yield uplift projects with measurable throughput and cash-flow benefits.

text_content: **Lean Opportunity Portfolio and Financial Impact Projection (FY 2026 Run-Rate)**

The lean opportunity portfolio targets a 1.4-day cycle-time reduction at Plant C and a +4.0 percentage-point first-pass yield uplift by 2026-12-31.
